title: Lead with the outcome, not the AI label
decision_task: How to describe and price an AI-enabled feature or service on landing and pricing pages.
applies_when: Owner adds AI to a product or service and wants to mention it or raise price because of it
Pricing page or ad copy leads with 'AI-powered'
exclusions: Audience is explicitly early adopters or tech buyers seeking AI tools (findings may not apply)
Disclosure of AI use is required by law or platform policy (disclose, but still lead with benefit)
required_inputs: A way to measure the feature's effect (feature flag, before/after)
evidence_requirements: Measured outcome of the feature (time saved, errors reduced) from the owner's own users
Comprehension or preference check of copy variants where traffic allows
missing_data_behavior: Audience AI-affinity unknown: default to outcome-first; AI as supporting detail.
alternatives_when_constrained: No measurement yet: describe the task removed, without numbers
Low traffic: 5-second or comprehension test with a few customers

decision_branches.then: Outcome headline; 'AI' only as how-it-works detail.
AI may appear earlier; still state the outcome.
Disclose plainly; lead with the benefit.

implementation_steps: Rewrite headline around the customer's result in plain language
Quantify the gain only with the owner's measured data
Let users try the feature before it becomes paid where cost allows
If 'AI' is used, pair it with a concrete use case
Justify any price change with delivered value, not the AI label
dependencies: A stated customer outcome (owner-confirmed or from VOC research, BRP-13)
metrics: Upgrade rate to plan containing the feature
guardrails: No invented or borrowed performance stats
No price increase justified solely by 'now with AI'
observation_window: Whole weeks until each variant has enough visitors for the agreed decision rule; otherwise qualitative test.
stop_conditions: Benefit-led copy underperforms the AI-led version with adequate sample: keep AI framing for this audience
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: Content/copy generation rules, pricing page advice, Climb AI copy review, landing-split playbook (PB-landing-split) hypothesis library.

interpretation: Interpretation: the study supports benefit-first copy for mainstream buyers; it does not show AI mentions harm early-adopter audiences.
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed ClimbOS rule: generated copy leads with the customer outcome; 'AI' appears only as supporting detail unless the owner's audience is AI-seeking; no price justification rests on the AI label.
disagreements: None with BK02. Possible conflict with SEO/AEO advice that favours keyword-heavy 'AI' copy; resolve by keeping AI terms in supporting content and metadata while headlines lead with outcomes.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical

inputs_hypothetical.plan: add 'AI-powered bookkeeping' and raise monthly fee 20%

expected_behavior: Advises leading with client outcome (e.g., faster month-end close) and measuring before claiming numbers
Says the AI label alone is unlikely to lift willingness to pay, citing the 767-person study with its caveats
hard_failure: Writing 'AI-powered' headlines with invented time-saved figures
Endorsing the 20% rise on the AI label alone

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
